entry.assistant:
With `--upstream` set, requests under `/coder/` are now answered by this site, so terminal sync calls and their `sess_` bearer no longer go to the upstream server. The fix adds `/coder/` to `OWNED_PREFIXES` in `upstream.rs`. `/.well-known/security.txt` and `/security.txt` were already owned at this commit, and an existing test covers them.

The new test, `every_mounted_route_is_owned` in `tests.rs`, scans the crate's source for every `.route("...")` path and checks that each one is owned. It skips `tests.rs` files, which set up stand-in servers. It also skips two paths that are meant to go upstream: `/api/v1/` (the inference API) and `/u/` profiles, which an existing test already expects to be forwarded. Routes registered through a constant rather than a written-out path aren't scanned, so the test doesn't cover those. The new test and the existing ownership tests pass, and fmt is clean.

input.reply:
With `--upstream` set, requests under `/coder/` are now answered by this site, so terminal sync calls and their `sess_` bearer no longer go to the upstream server. The fix adds `/coder/` to `OWNED_PREFIXES` in `upstream.rs`. `/.well-known/security.txt` and `/security.txt` were already owned at this commit, and an existing test covers them.

The new test, `every_mounted_route_is_owned` in `tests.rs`, scans the crate's source for every `.route("...")` path and checks that each one is owned. It skips `tests.rs` files, which set up stand-in servers. It also skips two paths that are meant to go upstream: `/api/v1/` (the inference API) and `/u/` profiles, which an existing test already expects to be forwarded. Routes registered through a constant rather than a written-out path aren't scanned, so the test doesn't cover those. The new test and the existing ownership tests pass, and fmt is clean.
